payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image visibly have a chalk-like drawing medium or surface treatment?
node.criteria: pass: visible chalk-like marks or texture establish a chalk medium; fail: the image is clearly rendered in a non-chalk medium with no visible chalk treatment; unknown: the medium cannot be determined from the image.
node.binding: Assess only visible evidence that the image uses a chalk-like medium or treatment.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image has a visibly grainy, smudged, chalk-like surface treatment across the scene, with softened sketchy outlines and textured shading.

n3: The node’s aggregation rule is too permissive for the rubric: it maps two passing feature checks directly to complete/yes, but the edited image still retains recognizable photographic detail and appears only partially converted to a chalk drawing. Preserve the separate chalk-medium and drawing-form evidence, but make the final decision assess whether the requested transformation is complete, not merely whether both features are detectable. Treat partial visual conversion as partial progress; do not infer completion from high-confidence support labels alone. Keep the rule grounded in the saved evidence and distinguish genuine visual incompleteness from transport or dependency failures.
n2: The node’s binding is appropriately limited to drawing form, but its pass criterion is too easy to satisfy: visible outlines and a sketch-like appearance can coexist with substantial photographic rendering. Keep medium assessment separate, yet make this support check distinguish a broadly transformed illustrated image from localized or superficial drawing effects, using the saved image evidence across the subjects and background. Here, the giraffes have pronounced drawn contours, while the scene retains photographic-looking texture and detail; record that mixed evidence rather than treating any detectable drawing cues as decisive proof of complete conversion. Do not turn this support node into the final completion judgment or infer absence of progress from uncertainty. The trace is valid and has no dependency or transport failure, so address visual criterion sensitivity, not execution plumbing.
